## Exercise 12.2

```{python}
import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "12-1-example.py"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,

result.check_returncode()
```

If I understand correctly. The evolution from MapReduce to Spark can be explained ... 
The MapReduce supposes relatively simple process. like one or two step aggregating process. 
But as time goes, the task is goign ot be complex, then saving and loading intermediate results is now bottleneck.
So there was a motivation to fit in this complex situation removing the bottleneck.

Then Spark comes, the core innovation is proposing RDD, which handles intermediate results more efficiently. 
It doesn't save and load, now the challenge here is the fault torrelance.  

So this RDD ensures immutability. patition level recovering. by doing that it can make so called lineage that is used efficient recovering from fault.
